description: a 12-person fintech, the week before an audit

business.name: Northwind Ledger
business.description: Northwind Ledger sells embedded treasury and reconciliation to mid-market logistics and freight companies — about 40 customers, all on annual contracts. Their first SOC 2 Type II audit starts fieldwork on Monday, three quarters of the evidence is still half-collected, and the two people who know where everything lives are also the two people carrying the Vantage Freight escalation.

cast.name: Priya Raman
cast.voice: Writes in tight, decisive paragraphs and always ends with who is doing what by when. Drops greetings entirely when she is behind, which this week she is.

cast.name: Marcus Bell
cast.voice: Long, warm, slightly rambling emails sent between 22:00 and midnight. Buries the actual ask in the fourth paragraph and signs off 'M'.

cast.name: Dana Okafor
cast.voice: Numbers first, no adjectives. Answers in bullet points and will say 'that number is wrong' without softening it. Unfailingly reliable on dates.

cast.name: Tomas Ruiz
cast.voice: Three-word fragments in Slack, careful and thorough in email. Says 'looking' and then vanishes for two hours. Hates being volunteered for meetings.

cast.name: Aisha Nkemdirim
cast.voice: Precise and slightly formal, numbers every point, apologises for length and then writes more. Flags risk early and repeats it until someone answers.

cast.name: Gerald Pike
cast.voice: Polite, clipped, entirely immovable on deadlines. Uses 'kindly' and numbered lists, and never acknowledges an excuse — he simply restates the request.

cast.name: Sofie Lind
cast.voice: Direct, a little clipped when annoyed, which is now. Short paragraphs, concrete amounts and times, and an explicit deadline in every message.

cast.name: Ravi Chandra
cast.voice: Relentlessly upbeat, three exclamation marks per email, always 'circling back'. Never answers the pricing question directly.

threads.subject: Vantage Freight — settlement timing, need an answer today

messages.body:
Priya,

Our Tuesday settlement landed 31 hours late again. That is the third time in six weeks and this one held up 214 driver payments. I have our board asking me directly whether Northwind is the right partner.

I need two things: what happened, and what changes so it does not happen a fourth time. Not a status page link.

Sofie

Sofie — acknowledged, and I am sorry. Tomas is pulling the timeline on the Tuesday batch now. I will have you a written answer with the actual cause and the fix by Thursday morning, not a status page.

Priya

It is Thursday. I have a 3pm with our CFO and I would rather walk in with your explanation than without it.

If the answer is that you do not know yet, tell me that and I will manage it — but tell me something by 2.

Priya, Aisha,

Following the walkthrough, the following remain outstanding:

1. Q2 user access review, signed
2. Change management tickets for the June release, with approver
3. Vendor risk assessments for the four subprocessors listed in the SOC description
4. Evidence of quarterly backup restoration testing

Kindly have these in the portal before fieldwork opens Monday.

Gerald Pike
Halloran & Pike

Gerald, Priya,

Status, in his numbering:

1. Done — uploaded, needs Priya's signature, that is the only blocker.
2. Partially. Eleven of the fourteen June tickets have a named approver. Three do not and Tomas is the only person who can reconstruct them.
3. Three of four. Ledgerlink has not returned their questionnaire despite two chases.
4. Not started. I am sorry to raise it this late — the restore test was scheduled for July and did not happen.

Item 4 is the one that worries me. Aisha

Thank you. To be clear: item 4 cannot be remediated retrospectively. If no restoration test was performed in the period, we will record it as a deficiency and I would rather you hear that now than on Monday.

Items 1 to 3 kindly land before end of day Friday.

Gerald

threads.subject: Ledgerlink renewal — the number moved again

messages.body:
Hi Priya!!

Great catching up last week! Circling back on the renewal — I have the paperwork ready to go whenever you are. Excited to keep building together!!

Ravi

Ravi — before anything gets signed I need the annual number in writing, and I need your security questionnaire back. Aisha has chased it twice. Both of those before we talk paperwork.

Priya

Totally hear you!! Working on the questionnaire with our security team — should be days not weeks.

On commercials, the renewal comes in at 68k which is a small uplift on last year but reflects the added volume. Happy to jump on a call!! Ravi

threads.subject: Board pack, draft 3 — the churn slide

messages.body:
Hi both,

Hope the week is being kind. I have been going back and forth on the board pack and I think draft 3 is close — the narrative on the treasury attach rate is much stronger, and the roadmap slide finally reads like a plan rather than a wish list.

One thing that has been nagging at me is that we present net retention at 104% while the churn slide shows two logos leaving in the same quarter. I do not think it is wrong, exactly, but I think Elena will ask, and I would rather we answer it than get asked.

Could one of you sanity check that pairing before Friday? M

104% is right. It is expansion on the top ten covering the two departures, both of which were sub-15k. The slides are not wrong, they are just next to each other.

I will add a footnote. Dana

threads.subject: Restore test — can we still do one this week

messages.body:
Tomas — Gerald has told us a missed restore test in the period is a deficiency and cannot be fixed after the fact. I want to be sure that is true for our case before we accept it.

Question: did anyone restore from backup during an incident between April and June? An unplanned restore that we can evidence counts. I have a memory of the May 14 database rollback but no ticket.

1. If yes, we need the ticket or the pager log.
2. If no, we run one today anyway so the next period is clean.

Aisha
